item.title: As millions of kids lose SNAP food benefits, free school meals are also at risk
item.description: Food stamps have a direct link to other critical resources, such as free breakfast and lunch at school. Now, experts say they're starting to see that link break.
item.content:encoded:
Food stamps have a direct link to other critical resources, such as free breakfast and lunch at school. Now, experts say they're starting to see that link break.

item.title: He tried to eliminate FEMA. Now he says the Trump administration has changed course
item.description: David Richardson worked to eliminate the country's top disaster agency when he led FEMA last year. Now, he says the administration has abandoned that goal.
item.content:encoded:
David Richardson worked to eliminate the country's top disaster agency when he led FEMA last year. Now, he says the administration has abandoned that goal.

item.title: Democrats demand Homeland Security officials fund election security ahead of midterms
item.description: The lawmakers wrote that they share "grave concern that time is running out … to assist state and local election officials in protecting our elections from cyber and mis-and disinformation threats."

item.title: Xi visits Egypt as China seeks deeper influence across the Mideast
item.description: China's President Xi Jinping visits Egypt this week for the first time in a decade. The trip illustrates China's growing ambitions at a time when U.S. influence has been weakened by its war in Iran.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Ex-Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and wife seek to end drug charges case on immunity grounds
item.description: Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife have asked a judge to dismiss the drug trafficking indictment against them on the grounds that they have immunity as the leader and first lady of a foreign country

item.title: NBA suspends Clippers owner Ballmer, fines team $30M, Kawhi Leonard $700K in cap circumvention case
item.description: Los Angeles Clippers owner Steve Ballmer was suspended for one year by the NBA, and the team was ordered to pay $30 million for violating salary cap circumvention rules in a case involving Kawhi Leonard.

item.title: Cassandra Wilson, Grammy-winning jazz vocalist, dies at 70
item.description: Wilson, whose deep, dark contralto was one of the most distinctive voices in jazz, died on Wednesday in her hometown of Jackson, Miss.

item.title: The IRS slashed its staff. One result? More taxes going uncollected
item.description: The IRS slashed its auditing staff last year — but the move may have backfired as tax collections from enforcement efforts plummeted, an Inspector General report shows.

item.title: A jury in Malta acquits a businessman in the killing of reporter Daphne Caruana Galizia
item.description: Investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia had written extensively about suspected corruption in political and business circles in Malta. She was killed by a car bomb in 2017, at age 53.

item.title: Olivia Rodrigo's women-led Daisy Chain Fields festival put the power in fans' hands
item.description: The inaugural edition of Rodrigo's one-day, women-led concert, which featured artists like Stevie Nicks, Sarah McLachlan and Chappell Roan, didn't sideline its stated political mission.
